_comment: Measured negatives from before this loop existed, seeded so the critic can refuse a
re-derivation with a receipt instead of the planner spending a call rediscovering them.
These are recorded under a SYNTHETIC HISTORICAL EPOCH on purpose. recall() marks any
cross-epoch record stale and render_context prints 'STALE EPOCH ... the NUMBER is not
comparable' -- which is exactly right: these were measured on a different anchor and a
different build recipe, so the MECHANISM knowledge transfers and the magnitude does not.
A seeded negative is a reason to say what is different, never a reason not to look.

records.statement: Async weight prefetch / LDS double-buffering in the dense Q8_0 GEMV hides HBM DMA latency and raises achieved bandwidth (GGML_CUDA_Q8_PREFETCH, compiled-in, runtime 0=off / 1=cached-DMA / 2=SLC-streaming).
records.falsifier: Decode throughput fails to rise on dense Q8 models with prefetch enabled.
records.reason: REJECTED 2026-07-11 on MI210, llama-bench base decode, r5, graphs ON, all 4 Q8 models. Net-negative and it hurts the DENSE models most despite targeting dense GEMV: Qwen3.6-27B dense -12%/-18%, gemma4-31B dense -6%/-7.5%. MoE marginal and sign-inconsistent (gemma4-A4B -3.5%/-0.3%, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B +4.2%/+3.1%), i.e. near noise. The prefetch/LDS-double-buffer overhead outweighs DMA-latency hiding on gfx90a at these shapes. Source: handoffs/active/gemma-challenge-kernel-techniques-v7.md.

records.statement: A fan-out / stream-reorder pass over the captured CUDA graph raises decode throughput (GGML_CUDA_GRAPH_OPT=1).
records.falsifier: Decode throughput fails to rise with the reorder pass enabled.
records.reason: REJECTED on MI210, measured net-negative: gemma4-A4B Q8 base decode -16% (68.8 vs 82.5 t/s), Q8 spec-dec ~-11% (~96 vs 108); Q4 spec-dec noisy/neutral. Left OFF (the default). Source: handoffs/active/gemma-challenge-kernel-techniques-v7.md.

records.statement: The CUDA graph cache is keyed by nodes[0] POINTER only, so the draft forward and each verify forward collide on one slot and pay a per-switch warmup reset; mixing an FNV-1a shape signature (per-node op + ne[], excluding data pointers) into the key gives each batch shape its own warm slot.
records.falsifier: With the shape key enabled, decode throughput does not rise on the Q8 focus quant.
records.reason: IMPLEMENTED env-gated and measured NEUTRAL, not landed. Clean re-eval (quiet card, strictly sequential, fresh server per run, single request; 3/3 reps byte-identical): Q8 spec-dec 107.2 vs 109.5 t/s (-2%) with output BYTE-IDENTICAL to default, so the change is numerically transparent but gives no speedup. Q4 spec-dec +6% but Q4 stayed noisy (2 output variants), not conclusive. Note the collision itself is UNCONFIRMED: the [SHAPE_KEY] keylog never fired because backend GGML_LOG_INFO is filtered during decode. Patch preserved at /mnt/raid0/llm/llama.cpp-experimental/lever-a-shape-key.patch. Revisit only if a profile shows verify re-capture is a MEASURED bottleneck, and fix the keylog to fprintf(stderr) first. Source: handoffs/active/gemma-challenge-kernel-techniques-v7.md.

records.statement: At batch-1 long context the KV read adds materially to bytes/token, so q8_0 KV-quant (-ctk/-ctv q8_0, -fa 1) raises single-stream decode throughput.
records.falsifier: q8-KV decode at 64k single-stream does not beat f16-KV outside the noise band.
records.target_surface: runtime flag (-ctk/-ctv), not a kernel patch
records.reason: FALSIFIED 2026-08-14 on frozen v9 (0db32c06e / 10125), observation-grade, 64k single-stream: 35B-A3B GDN hybrid 75.8 -> 63.1 t/s (-16.7%), dense 27B 21.7 -> 20.2 t/s (-6.9%). The dequant cast cost exceeds the KV bandwidth saving even on the dense 27B (all-full-global KV, where the KV read most rivals weight bytes). Matches the CPU precedent that the dequant cast COSTS throughput. Note mi210-q8-dequant-gemv-roofline.md still lists this as an ALIVE Tier-3 lever (L8); it is not. Source: handoffs/active/fable5-window2-findings-05c-mi210-lever-category-matrix.md gap-list row L14.

records.statement: Grouping MMQ tile rows (workgroup-mapping / swizzle, the G17 +9.823% proxy result) raises L2 hit rate and MMQ throughput on the real decode surface.
records.falsifier: On the real batched decode tile grid, row-grouping does not raise L2 hit rate at flat read volume.
records.reason: MEASURED NEGATIVE and mechanistically explained. The +9.823% proxy used a SYMMETRIC 64x64 tile grid where row-grouping has real headroom; the real MMQ surface is a batched pp=32 / tg=8 / pl=128 / n_kv=5120 decode whose tile grid is strongly M-heavy. With few N tiles the DEFAULT linear order already captures full activation reuse in a short window, so grouping M by 8-32 can only ENLARGE the concurrently-resident weight footprint -- predicting hit rate DOWN at flat read volume, which is exactly the measured -7.455 pts at +0.201% reads. Reinforcing: the CDNA MMQ path is PERSISTENT STREAM-K and already owns tile assignment (the r1 pilot was a literal no-op because the remap sat outside that path), and Q4_K decode weights stream with WGM0 hit rate already at 67.304%. Source: handoffs/active/autokernel-research-loop.md section 23.1 finding F3.

records.statement: Building the llama.cpp HIP candidate against ROCm 10.1 (instead of 6.2) improves decode or prefill on MI210.
records.falsifier: Spec-off decode B/C < 1.05 on 2 valid ABBA pairs, or pp512@d16384 B/C < 1.00.
records.reason: MEASURED NO-GO on C6 729599d69, MI210. Spec-off decode B/C mean 0.9746 over 2 ABBA pairs (0.986, 0.963); pp512@d16384 B/C 0.789 (P), 0.769 (K2), 0.753 (K3), D256-cap and CDNA-tune knobs do not recover it. Top regressing family is a Tensile Cijk_Alik_Bljk_HSS MT128x96x64 GEMM present only on the 10.1 side. The earlier Stage-1 decode +8.7% (r2 median 1.087) was DRAFT ACCEPTANCE, not kernel speed. Ratio higher=better. A static audit looked good (spills 145->96, FA-MMA 53->2) and did not predict the runtime loss. Caveats: F0 cells invalid (-fa 0 with q8_0 KV cannot create a context), decision unaffected; only 2 valid pairs. Source: /mnt/raid0/llm/tmp/q38p3a-verdict.json, q38p3-r2-verdict.json, docs/reference/mi210-serving-program-findings-20261105.md. Evidence /mnt/raid0/llm/tmp/q38p3a-verdict.json (+ q38p3-r2-verdict.json). Measured on C6 729599d69 (2026-11-05), NOT this file's historical epoch: mechanism transfers, magnitude is cross-epoch.

records.statement: A GPU flat-PCA per-key top-k indexer feeding the H12 fused sparse FA beats dense FA on the 27B global layers at kv=32768.
records.falsifier: geomean dense_us/lsa_us at kv=32768 < 1.10 (flag ratio 1.1, 5 reps).
records.target_surface: ggml/src/ggml-cuda (QSA indexer + fused sparse FA, LSA-H12-INDEXER)
records.reason: MEASURED FUTILE on build 289207e31 (store gpu-20261106-289207e31-lsah12) vs C7 c420b9d1a, MI210. geomean dense/lsa at kv=32768 = 0.368 (lsa SLOWER). Cells dense_us/lsa_us -> ratio: kv32768 nb1 342.7/722.9=0.474, nb8 400.4/1269.2=0.315, nb16 519.7/1564.6=0.332, nb512 5482/14820=0.370; kv16384 nb512 0.202; kv65536 nb1 0.574. Ratio higher=better. Packet caveat: selection is a flat per-key PCA top-k (+ window 512, sinks 4), NOT the author Ward bucket selector (only the map and scorer math ported), so this refutes the flat-PCA-indexer variant, not Ward/bucketed LSA. Source: /mnt/raid0/llm/tmp/lsa-h12-indexer-gate-20261106/out/RESULT.json (perf.json, correct.json). Evidence /mnt/raid0/llm/tmp/lsa-h12-indexer-gate-20261106/out/RESULT.json. Measured on C7 (2026-11-06), not this file's historical epoch.

records.statement: An MFMA-based skinny Q8_0 GEMM (H16 family, kill-switched knob) speeds up the 27B verify-step matmuls at M=36 (np4 x 9) over C7r MMQ.
records.falsifier: Op-level verify-step matmul ratio base/new < 1.0 outside the keep-tail (futility stop before e2e).
records.target_surface: ggml/src/ggml-cuda (mmq / skinny Q8_0 matmul dispatch, gfx90a)
records.reason: MEASURED NO_KEEP_OP_FUTILE on candidate a60768af3 (store gpu-20261107-a60768af3-c8h16) vs C7r 62cb6a6af, MI210 gfx90a, row c8-h16-gate-20261107. Correctness passed on 5 suites; kill-switch parity 1.0018. Op-level M=36 verify-step matmul over the real 27B shape census (7 shapes, 407 matmuls): base/new = 0.8542 (effect -14.58%, keep_tail P 2.23% / F 3.15%, effect_inside_tail False, enforced), so a resolved loss; e2e never ran. Per-M geomean base/new: M12 0.802, M16 0.776, M18 0.839, M24 0.848, M27 0.810, M32 0.742, M36 0.890 (M9 reads 0.558 under the key geomean_base_over_h16, a differently named key). The slow cells are the large GEMMs (5120x17408@32 0.708, 5120x6144@32 0.612); only 6144x5120@36 won (1.109). Ratio higher=better (base/new). Do not re-propose an MFMA f16 skinny Q8_0 kernel for M 12..36 without a mechanism that explains the M=12..32 loss. Source: /mnt/raid0/llm/tmp/c8-h16-gate-20261107/out/RESULT.json keys /b/op_ratio_M36, /b/keep_tail, /b/per_M, /b/cases, /b/killsw_over_base_geomean, /verdict; root commit d3f97494f handoffs/active/kernel-champion-and-promotion.md (C8-2-H16-M36). Measured on C7r (2026-11-07), not this file's historical epoch.
